description: On 07 February 2025, the fishing vessel "FORTUNE PRIDE", with 4 people on board, sank off Sambro, NS. The crew abandoned the vessel. All crew members were recovered; two were pronounced deceased.
On 07 February 2025, the fishing vessel "FORTUNE PRIDE", with 4 people on board, sank off Sambro, NS. The crew abandoned the vessel. All crew members were recovered; two were pronounced deceased.
On 06 January 2025, the unmanned barge "OC38-B" was reported being partly submerged in a vicinity of the l'Île-aux-Tourtes Bridge in the Lake of Two Mountains off Vaudreuil-Dorion, QC.
On 24 December 2024, the tug "BROUGHTON RANGER", while uncrewed, was reported to have sunk alongside in Port Hardy, B.C.

On 24 November 2024, the tug "WESTCOASTER", with 2 people on board, reported that the barge it was towing, the "JENSEN COVE", was taking on water and listing in the vicinity of Christie Passage off Port Hardy, BC. The barge later capsized and sank. Minor pollution was reported.

On 16 November 2024, the fishing vessel "NICK & ASH 2021", with 4 people on board, was reported capsized in the Bay of Fundy off Grand Manan, NB. All crew members were rescued from the water by the fishing vessels "SCOTIA BAND IT" and "LAST HAUL", and transported to North Head, NB. The Canadian Coast Guard Ship "GELIGET" reported that the fishing vessel sank but remained partially submerged.

On 14 November 2024, the fishing vessel "IVY ROSE", with 6 people on board, reported being disabled and taking on water in the vicinity of the Grand Banks off St. Stephens, NL. The crew controlled the water ingress and the fishing vessel was assisted by the container vessel "GLASGOW EXPRESS" and the Canadian Coast Guard Ship "JEAN GOODWILL".

On 15 October 2022, an unregistered fishing vessel, with 2 people on board, was reported missing. The sunken vessel was found in Cockeram Lake, MB. After an extensive search both crew members were recovered and declared deceased.

On 21 October 2024, the fishing vessel "HUDSON & FINLEY", with 2 people on board, reported taking on water with unserviceable bilge pumps at the mouth of Sheet Harbour, NS. The crew was able to restart 2 pumps while being towed into the harbour by a recreational craft.
On 01 October 2024, the unmanned workboat "C14307BC" sunk while secured in Maple Ridge, BC. Minor pollution was reported.

On 16 July 2024, the fishing vessel "SNOW QUEEN", with 5 people on board, reported taking on water in its engine room while proceeding in Chatham Sound off Lax Kw'alaams, BC. The crew pumped water out while proceeding to Port Edwards, BC.

On 17 June 2024, an unregistered fishing vessel, with 3 people on board, took on water and sank while its crew were hauling back fishing nets on Lake Winnipeg, MB. All 3 crew members ended up in the water without personal flotation devices. Subsequent search and rescue efforts rescued 2 crew members and recovered 1 deceased.

On 31 May 2024, the unoccupied Canadian Coast Guard workboat "C23572QC" was reported having capsized while being recovered by the Canadian Coast Guard Ship "A. LEBLANC" in the Gulf of St. Lawrence off Grande-Entrée, QC. The workboat was recovered and the "A. LEBLANC" proceeded to Cap-aux-Meules, QC for a damage assessment of its workboat.

On 27 May 2024, the fishing vessel "MALBAIE STAR I", with 5 people on board, reported having capsized in Baie de Gaspé, QC. All crew members were recovered by the fishing vessel "OCEAN OUTLAW" and transported to Grande-Grave, QC for medical assistance. The vessel subsequently sank and the wreck was later secured by the Canadian Coast Guard Ship "CAP AUX MEULES".

On 21 May 2024, the fishing vessel "MISS PIG BROOK", with 3 people on board, reported taking on water in Northumberland Strait off Fox Harbour, NS. The vessel was assisted to Wallace Harbour, NS by the Canadian Coast Guard auxiliary vessel "NOVEMBER RAIN".

On 17 May 2024, the unnamed fishing vessel known as "VRN 140660" was reported capsized on a shoal off Port au Choix, NL, with no one in the vicinity of the wreck and debris on scene. The Search and Rescue authorities later confirmed that all 3 crew members reached the shore safely.

On 17 May 2024, the fishing vessel "ATLANTIC GALE", with 6 people on board, reported taking on water while in the vicinity of Western Bradelle Valley, QC. The crew controlled the ingress and the vessel proceeded to Shippagan, NB for repairs.

On 09 May 2024, the Canadian Coast Guard Ship "SPRAY", with 4 people on board, reported taking on water off Bonavista Bay, NL. The vessel was escorted to its base station in Old Perlican, NL by the Canadian Coast Guard auxiliary vessel "ATLANTIC MAVERICK".

On 08 May 2024, the fishing vessel "LADY ERICA", with 2 people on board, was reported taking on water with a bilge pump failure in Northumberland Strait off Souris, PE. The vessel was assisted by the Canadian Coast Guard Ship "CAPE SPRY" and escorted to Launching Place, PE.

On 07 May 2024, the fishing vessel "PROVOCANTE", with 3 people on board, was reported taking on water and having intentionally ran aground in Miscou Channel, NB. Two crew members were evacuated on the beach. The master remained on board and proceeded away from the shore while assisted by fishing vessels in the area. The vessel was towed to Miscou, NB by the fishing vessel "LE P'TIT COTIER".

On 21 April 2024, after landing 4 people on the shore, an unnamed dory, with 2 people on board, was reported capsized with its crew members overboard in the vicinity of Port au Port Bay, NL. The four people stranded ashore were evacuated to Lark Harbour, NL by helicopter, and the two crew members in the water were recovered, and later pronounced deceased.

On 07 April 2024, the fishing vessel "KIJU", with 7 people on board, reported being disabled with an ingress of water in its engine room in the Gulf of St. Lawrence in the vicinity of Banc Bradelle, QC. The water ingress was controlled and the vessel was towed to Shippegan, NB by the Canadian Coast Guard Ship "CAP BRETON".

On 03 April 2024, the fishing vessel "MARIE-EVE", with 5 people on board, reported being disabled with water ingress in its engine room in the vicinity of Miscou Banks, NB. The vessel was towed to Shippegan, NB by the Canadian Coast Guard Ships "BAIE DE PLAISANCE" and "CAP BRETON".

On 24 January 2024, the fishing vessel "JALEMA C.", with 2 people on board, was reported taking on water in the Bay of Fundy off Saint John, NB. Both crew members were recovered by the fishing vessel "SITANSISK II" and transported to Chance Harbour, NB. The vessel capsized and then sank.

On 24 January 2024, the fishing vessel "JALEMA C.", with 2 people on board, was reported taking on water in the Bay of Fundy off Saint John, NB. Both crew members were recovered by the fishing vessel "SITANSISK II" and transported to Chance Harbour, NB. The vessel capsized and then sank.

On 24 January 2024, the fishing vessel "JALEMA C.", with 2 people on board, was reported taking on water in the Bay of Fundy off Saint John, NB. Both crew members were recovered by the fishing vessel "SITANSISK II" and transported to Chance Harbour, NB. The vessel capsized and then sank.

On 10 January 2024, the workboat "C12972BC", with 4 people on board, reported taking on water after a wave broke its bridge windows in Queen Charlotte Strait, BC. The crew abandoned the vessel before it sank, and were recovered from the water by the Canadian Coast Guard Ship "PORT HARDY I" and assisted by the "FLORENCIA BAY", the "SIR WILFRED GRENFELL" and the "COASTAL SERVER". All crew members were carried to Port Hardy, BC to receive medical assistance.

On 07 January 2024, the fishing vessel "NORTHERN OSPREY III", with 30 people on board, reported taking on water in Porcupine Bay, NL. The vessel was anchored and temporary repairs were effected. Assistance was provided by the Royal Canadian Air Force helicopter "RESCUE 901"and the fishing vessel "KATSHESHUK II", until the Canadian Coast Guard Ship "TELEOST" arrived with divers who completed repairs. The vessel then proceeded to St. John's, NL.

On 04 December 2023, the fishing vessel "THUNDERCAT", with 4 people on board, reported taking on water in the Gulf of Maine off Westport, NS. The vessel was assisted and escorted to Sandford, NS by the Canadian Coast Guard Ship "SAMBRO".

On 04 December 2023, the fishing vessel "SMOOTH MOVER", with 4 people on board, reported taking on water off Wedgeport, NS. The vessel was assisted and escorted to Clark's Harbour, NS by the Canadian Coast Guard Ship "CHEDABUCTO BAY".

On 02 December 2023, the fishing vessel "PERSEVERANCE 2014", with 4 people on board, reported taking on water off Yarmouth, NS. The crew was assisted by the Canadian Coast Guard Ship "SAMBRO" and resumed its voyage.

On 23 October 2023, the unregistered tug known as "GREEN HORNET", with 1 person on board, reported having capsized in the Strait of Georgia off Vancouver, BC. The Search and Rescue response team found the crew member deceased on shore. The vessel sank, but was later retrieved and taken to a drydock in Mill Bay, BC.

On 11 October 2023, the unregistered fishing vessel known as "WANDA LYNN", with 2 people on board, reported taking on water and being at risk of sinking in St. Marys Bay off Little Brook, NS. The Canadian Coast Guard Ship "WESTPORT" and its workboat assisted the vessel. The 2 crew members were recovered and carried to Saulnierville, NS by the fishing vessel "BETH AND JANE". The disabled vessel was later reported aground and a salvage plan was established.

On 22 September 2023, the fishing vessel "CAPIEN DES MERS", with 3 people on board, reported taking on water in Détroit d'Honguedo off L'Anse-au-Griffon, QC. The vessel proceeded to L'Anse-au-Griffon, QC, and was provided with additional pumps to assist with dewatering.

On 25 September 2023, the fishing vessel "SILVER CONDOR", with 6 people on board, sank in the St. Lawrence River off Gros-Mécatina, QC. All crew members were recovered from the water by the helicopter "RESCUE 901" and by the Canadian Coast Guard Ship "CAPE EDENSHAW" and were brought to Corner Brook, NL to receive medical assistance.

On 13 September 2023, the light tug "SANDRA MARY", with 2 people on board, reported taking on water in Cabot Strait off Glace Bay, NS. The crew controlled the water ingress and received assistance from the fishing vessel "POPPY'S ANGELS" and from a local Fisheries and Oceans workboat. The vessel was towed to North Sydney, NS by the Canadian Coast Guard Ship "LA POILE BAY".

On 12 September 2023, the unregistered fishing vessel known as "ROWIN' SAILOR" was reported to have sank with all 4 crew members in the water in Bishie Cove, NL. The Canadian Coast Guard Ships "CONCEPTION BAY", "EARL GREY" and "PENNANT BAY" were tasked to assist. One crew member was recovered by the pleasure craft "MORGAN AND TILLIA". Two bodies were later recovered by assisting vessels of opportunity and transferred to an ambulance ashore in Fleur de Lys, NL. One person is still missing.

On 28 August 2023, the fishing vessel "GRACE ABOUNDS", with 2 people on board, reported being disabled and taking on water in Placentia Bay, NL. The vessel was assisted and escorted to Davis Cove, NL by the fishing vessels "BOW DOWN 2021" and "AQUA ENDEAVOR", and by the Canadian Coast Guard Ship "W.G. GEORGE".
On 21 August 2023, the fishing vessel "SEA GAY", with no one on board, was reported to have sank while secured in Port Hardy, BC. The vessel was later removed from the marine environment.

On 27 July 2023, the fishing vessel "ZAPORA", with 2 people on board, reported taking on water and being at risk of sinking in Cascadia Basin, BC. The vessel was assisted by nearby fishing vessels and was escorted to Ucluelet, BC by the Canadian Coast Guard Ships "SIR JOHN FRANKLIN" and "CAPE MCKAY".

On 20 July 2023, the air cushion vehicle "L'ESPRIT-DE-PAKUASHIPI", with 5 people on board, reported being disabled with a total failure of its engine and water ingress in its engine room in Rivière Saint-Augustin, QC. The barge "RIVIERE SAINT-AUGUSTIN" took the crew members on board and towed the vessel to Saint-Augustin, QC to assess damages.

On 24 July 2023, the fishing vessel "C25493BC" known as "WESTERN SLOPE", with 1 person on board, was reported having capsized in Okanagan Lake off Vernon, BC. The vessel was retrieved and the crew member was reported as missing.

On 07 July 2023, the crew boat "C32388BC", with 6 people on board, reported taking on water in Chatham Channel, BC. The crew abandoned the vessel in a zodiac while the vessel was sinking. All crew members were evacuated to Lagoon Cove, BC by a vessel of opportunity.

On 11 July 2023, the fishing vessel "ADDIE N' AINSLIE", with 7 people on board, reported taking on water and being at risk of sinking on The Grand Banks of Newfoundland, NL. The crew abandoned the vessel in a liferaft and was recovered by the container ship "INDEPENDENT QUEST". The crew was then transferred on the fishing vessel "KATSHESHUK II" and finally on the Canadian Coast Guard Ship "CAPE ROGER" to proceed to St. John's, NL. The disabled vessel was reported sank.

On 05 July 2023, the fishing vessel "MISS NANCY I", with 2 people on board and while being towed by the fishing vessel "OCEAN ROVER", was reported taking on water in the Strait of Georgia, BC. Commercial towing assistance was provided for the vessel to proceed to Steveston, BC.
On 23 June 2023, an unnamed and unregistered dozer tug was reported to have sunk in Powell Lake, BC. The sunken tug was later refloated and salvaged.

On 26 June 2023, the fishing vessel "MAX 'D OUT", with 5 people on board, reported taking on water in Northumberland Strait off Red Point, PE. The Canadian Coast Guard Ship "CAPE SPRY" provided assistance and then escorted the vessel to Souris, PE.
On 05 October 2022, the unmanned loaded barge "YSAMARIE", while under tow by the tug "ETOILE SIRIUS", was reported to have capsized and sunk in the Gulf of St. Lawrence off Gaspé, QC.

On 29 May 2023, the fishing vessel "SEA GAY", with no one on board, was reported taking on water and being at risk of sinking at a wharf in Port Hardy, BC. The fuel and water were pumped out and the source of the ingress was investigated.

On 21 May 2023, an unknown landing barge, with no one on board, was reported taking on water while secured at a wharf in Port Alberni, BC. Measures were taken by the harbour authorities to control a minor loss of pollutants.

On 24 May 2023, the tender of the fishing vessel "OCEAN BILLOW II", with no one on board, was reported sunken off Petty Harbour, NL by an aircraft. The fishing vessel "CONCEPTION RUN" and an aircraft positively identified the sunken vessel.

On 17 May 2023, the fishing vessel "CRACK CORN", with 5 people on board, reported taking on water in the engine room while proceeding in Louisbourg Harbour, NS. The vessel was assisted by a Canadian Coast Guard workboat to proceed to a wharf in Louisbourg, NS and solve the issue alongside.

On 17 May 2023, the fishing vessel "CRACK CORN", with 5 people on board, reported taking on water in the engine room while proceeding in Louisbourg Harbour, NS. The vessel was assisted by a Canadian Coast Guard workboat to proceed to a wharf in Louisbourg, NS and solve the issue alongside.

On 10 May 2023, the fishing vessel "DAUPHIN III", with 1 person on board, reported taking on water in the engine room while alongside in Rimouski, QC. The water was pumped out and repairs were effected.

On 11 May 2023, an unknown barge, towed by the fishing vessel "SOUTHERLY SACRIFICE", was reported taking on water and at risk of sinking in the Bay of Fundy off Westport, NS. The vessel disconnected from the barge and sank before the arrival of the Canadian Coast Guard Ship "SAMBRO".

On 09 May 2023, the fishing vessel "OCEAN SURFER II", with 5 people on board, reported being beset in heavy ice conditions off La Scie, NL. The disabled vessel was freed by the Canadian Coast Guard Ship "ANN HARVEY" and escorted to La Scie, NL.

On 01 May 2023, an unnamed recreational craft, with hull number "BC8359554" and 2 people on board, was reported capsized on the shore of Yeo Islands in Ballenas Channel, BC. The passengers were evacuated by a vessel of opportunity.

On 26 April 2023, the fishing vessel "L'ECHO DES MERS I", with 1 person on board and carrying 300 litres of fuel, took on water while being towed by the fishing vessel "SIDEWINDER" near Hermitage Bay, NL. The person on board abandoned directly onto the "SIDEWINDER". The "L'ECHO DES MERS I" sank near the surface.
On 13 April 2023, the unregistered landing craft known as "MILLBANKE IV", with no one on board, was reported as partially sunk while moored at Ladysmith Harbour, BC.

On 15 April 2023, the fishing vessel "KIJU", with 7 people onboard, reported that it was disabled due to issues with its propeller shaft and that it was taking on water.   The KIJU was towed to Shippagan, NB, by the fishing vessel ''J.A.D JASMINE''.

On 17 April 2023, the tug "OMNI COASTAL", with 4 people onboard, reported that it ran aground and was taking on water near East Headland Island in Lake Ontario, ON. The crew was removed from the vessel and salvage operations were carried out.

On 12 April 2023, the fishing vessel "RAZOR'S EDGE I" with 3 persons onboard reported taking on water, the fishing vessels " BIG G" and "ATLANTIC RENEGADE" provided dewatering pumps and the vessel made it safely to LOCKEPORT, N.S.

On 25 February 2023, the tug "NORTH ARM PROWLER", while towing an unregistered barge, reported taking on water with a cracked hull and being at risk of sinking while proceeding in the Strait of Georgia, BC. The water was pumped out as the vessel proceeded to Powell River, BC to effect repairs.
On 16 February 2023, an unregistered workboat with no one on board was reported to have sunk in Fulford Harbour, BC. No pollution was observed at the time of the report.

On 04 February 2023, the fishing vessel "COLE & MORGAN", with 6 people on board, reported having sustained heavy freezing spray and icing conditions causing an ingress of water in the engine room off Guyon Island, NS. The vessel proceeded at slow speed to Louisbourg, NS and lost power near the wharf where it dropped anchor. A Canadian Coast Guard cutter assisted the vessel to reach the dock.

On 04 February 2023, the fishing vessel "COLE & MORGAN", with 6 people on board, reported having sustained heavy freezing spray and icing conditions causing an ingress of water in the engine room off Guyon Island, NS. The vessel proceeded at slow speed to Louisbourg, NS and lost power near the wharf where it dropped anchor. A Canadian Coast Guard cutter assisted the vessel to reach the dock.

On 30 January 2023, the fishing vessel "MIDNIGHT BANDIT", with 4 people on board, reported taking on water and being at risk of sinking while proceeding in The Gully, NS. The water was pumped out and the vessel was repaired at sea with the assistance of the fishing vessel "MISS ANNETTE". Once repaired, the vessel resumed its regular operations.

On 28 January 2023, an unknown crane barge, with 2 people on board and while being towed by the tug "ISLAND MASTER", was reported taking on water while alongside at the sailing club in Ganges Harbour, BC. The Canadian Coast Guard Ship "CAPE NADEN" assisted the vessel while the crew members found the leak and pumped the water out.

On 17 January 2023, the fishing vessel "ROPO", with no one on board, was reported to have sunk while moored in the harbour of Ahousat, BC. The vessel sank on 10 September 2022 while tied up to another fishing vessel which also sunk.

On 06 January 2023, the fishing vessel "DUBY C.", with no one on board, was reported as being at risk of sinking in Drew Harbour, BC. The owner attended the vessel and stabilized it. No water ingress was found.

On 12 December 2022, the fishing vessel "KNOT FOR SHORE", with 4 people on board, reported experiencing water ingress in its engine room in the Gulf of Maine off Yarmouth, NS. The crew effected repairs on the live well and resumed their fishing operations.

On 03 December 2022, the fishing vessel "SEA SONS II", with 1 person on board, reported having capsized while being towed by the fishing vessel "CAPE DOG ENDEAVOR" in Conception Bay off Cape St. Francis, NL. The crew member was evacuated from the vessel.

On 26 November 2022, the fishing vessel "GEORGIA ADDISON", with 5 people on board, reported experiencing water ingress off Glace Bay, NS. The vessel was towed to Sydney, NS by the Canadian Coast Guard Ship "SPINDRIFT".

On 17 November 2022, the tug "F.W. WRIGHT", with 3 people on board and while towing the barge "EVCO NO. 3", reported that the barge took on water and overturned in the Strait of Georgia off Gibsons, BC. The tug was able to continue towing the barge to English Bay, BC.
On 19 October 2022, the aquaculture vessel "THE BABY", with 3 people on board, reported having capsized in Georgetown Harbour, PE. All crew members were rescued by nearby aquaculture vessel "MB2".

On 07 November 2022, the workboat "COAST ISLE", with 1 person on board, capsized when assisting the spud barges "SALTAIR RIGGER" AND "ARROW PARK" in Fraser River, BC. The workboat was removed from the environment with the assistance of divers.

On 24 October 2022, the fishing vessel "JACOB LOUISA", with 9 people on board, reported taking on water in Hamilton Bank off Cartwright, NL. The vessel proceeded under its own power to Charlottetown, NL.

On 28 September 2022, the fishing vessel "OLD COW" reported taking on water in Northumberland Strait off Pictou Island, NS. The fishing vessel "CHASING SEAS" and a Pictou Fisheries Patrol Vessel escorted the vessel to Caribou, NS.
On 12 September 2022, the Canadian Coast Guard Ship "CAPTAIN MOLLY KOOL" reported flooding and listing to port by 5 degrees due to unintentional flooding in the drydock in St. John's, NL.

On 06 September 2022, the fishing vessel "SEA PRO", with 3 people on board, reported taking on water in Northumberland Strait off Saint-Édouard-de-Kent, NB. The fishing vessel "PURE COMFORT" escorted the vessel to Richibucto, NB.

On 10 September 2022, the passenger vessel "ISLAND BAY", with 7 people on board, reported sinking in Carpenter Bay near Moresby Island, BC, in heavy weather. While those on board were abandoning the vessel into the lifeboat, 2 passengers went overboard. They were immediately recovered. Minor pollution was reported. The vessel was subsequently recovered.

On 06 September 2022, the fishing vessel "STRIKER", with 1 person on board, reported taking on water and being at risk of sinking in Gabriola Passage off Gabriola Island, BC. The commercial towing vessel "SILVA BAY" towed the fishing vessel to a marina in Nanaimo, BC.

On 05 September 2022, the barge "DELTA PRINCESS" reported taking on water and being at risk of sinking in the middle arm of the Fraser River off Sea Island, BC. After an inspection, a hole was identified in the midship bottom hull section and temporary repairs were carried out.

On 29 August 2022, a recreational ski boat reported being at risk of sinking from the wake caused by the passing tugs "SAAM VENTA", "SST SALISH" and "TRIDENT WARRIOR" in Vancouver Harbour off Burnaby, BC. One of the 2 people on the ski boat suffered a minor injury.

On 03 August 2022, the Canadian Coast Guard service vessel "PRIVATE ROBERTSON V.C.", with no one on board and while moored, reported taking on water and being at risk of sinking in Patricia Bay, BC. Repairs were effected to rectify the issues.

On 08 August 2022, the fishing vessel "GYPSY MARINER", with 7 persons on board, reported taking on water approximately 60 nautical miles east of St. John's, NL. The crew abandoned the vessel before it sank and were rescued by the offshore supply vessel "ATLANTIC GRIFFON".
On 03 August 2022, the cargo barge "CRT-001" was reported to be sinking and having run aground in Hudson Bay off Inukjuak, QC. No pollution was reported.

On 30 July 2022, the fishing vessel "P.E. 260" reported being at a risk of sinking while at a local dock in Port Edward, BC. With the assistance from a Canadian Coast Guard Ship, the "P.E. 260" was stabilized. Minor pollution was reported.

On 15 June 2022, the workboat "C29603BC", known as "TRUCKER II" with 3 people on board, while attempting to tow a log took on water and sank in Gravesend Reach, Fraser River, BC. The 3 people on board were rescued from the water by another nearby workboat.

On 14 July 2022, the unregistered aquaculture vessel, with 4 people on board, reported taking on water and capsized in Lewis Channel off Cortes Island, BC. The Canadian Coast Guard Inshore Rescue Boat "509" rescued the 4 people and the vessel was secured to shore.

On 11 July 2022, the unregistered fishing vessel known as "ROBERT BRIAN", with no one on board, was reported to have capsized and sank in Alberni Inlet off Hocking Point, BC. Resulting pollution was contained with sorbents.

On 23 June 2022, the landing craft "PALAQUIN" was reported taking on water and being at a risk of sinking while anchored in Silva Bay off Sear Island, BC. The vessel was stabilized and towed to Degnen Bay, BC.

On 28 June 2022, the fishing vessel "ASHLEY AND BROTHERS", with 5 people on board, reported taking on water while out to sea off St. Anthony, NL. The Cormorant helicopter R912 and the Canadian Coast Guard Ship "PENNANT BAY" were tasked and multiple fishing vessels responded to the mayday broadcast. The water ingress was stopped and the vessel was towed to St. Anthony, NL.

On 20 June 2022, the herring fishing vessel "SEALIFE II", with 5 people on board, reported its herring skiff as capsized, with 2 people on board, in the Gulf of Maine off Grand Manan Island, NB. The 2 crew members were recovered from the water and transported by the vessel "BRUNSWICK PROVIDER" to Seal Cove, NB for medical care.

On 19 June 2022, the turbot fishing vessel "BACCALIEU ENDEAVOUR", with 6 people on board, reported taking on water while out at sea off Cape Bonavista, NL. The pumps on board removed the water ingress as the Canadian Coast Guard Ship "CAPTAIN MOLLY KOOL" escorted the vessel to Valleyfield, NL.

On 16 June 2022, the fishing vessel "GENERATION V", with 2 people on board, reported taking on water in Back Bay, NB and proceeding back to port. The United States Coast Guard tasked an aircraft to assist and the nearby vessel "FUNDY NAVIGATOR" escorted the vessel to port.

On 09 June 2022, the fishing vessel "DARCY DEAN" reported taking on water and being at risk of sinking in Canso Ledges, NS. The crew carried out repairs and the vessel resumed its voyage to Canso, NS while escorted by another fishing vessel.

On 03 June 2022, the herring carrier vessel "CAPELCO" reported taking on water and being at risk of sinking in Long Island Bay, NB. The crew carried out repairs and the vessel resumed its voyage to North Head, NB, escorted by another fishing vessel.

On 24 May 2022, the fishing vessel "DAD" reported taking on water in the Gulf of St. Lawrence off West Point, PE. The fishing vessel "PURE COMFORT" advised it was alongside the vessel in distress and provided assistance until the situation was stabilized.

On 04 May 2022, the passenger vessel "WILDERNESS LEGACY", while towing a skiff, reported its towline having departed in Discovery Passage near Willow Point, BC. The skiff capsized and was subsequently recovered. No pollution was recovered.

On 02 May 2022, the fishing vessel "OUR LEGACY", with 6 people on board, reported taking on water and being at risk of sinking in Notre Dame Bay, NL. The crew carried out repairs and the vessel was able to reach Triton, NL while escorted by the Canadian Coast Guard Ship "CONCEPTION BAY".

On 26 April 2022, the fishing vessel "DREAM CATCHER VI", with 4 people on board, reported water accumulating on its deck in the Gulf of St. Lawrence off Shippagan, NB. After the crew cleared its scuppers, the water was able to drain. The vessel cancelled its distress signal and resumed its voyage.

On 10 April 2022, the fishing vessel "L'ECHO DES MERS I", with 3 people on board, reported taking on water and being at risk of sinking, 25 nautical miles SSW of Fortune, NL. The fishing vessel "BRITTANY WAVE" attended to the vessel and provided additional pumps. Once the crew had carried out repairs, the vessel resumed its intended voyage.

On 25 March 2022, an unregistered tug, with no person on board and while docked, was reported to have sunk near the shore of Port Alberni, BC. The tug was retrieved, dewatered and refloated. Minor pollution was reported.

On 26 March 2022, the barge "SEASPAN 492", while being towed by the tug "HAISEA GUARDIAN", reported to have experienced a starboard list and beached intentionally to avoid sinking near Richmond, BC. The cargo was transferred to a rig and the barge was towed to Delta, BC to carry out repairs.
On 02 April 2022, the fishing vessel "YOHAN MIRJA" reported taking on water and being at risk of sinking in Sept-Îles, QC. The crew carried out repairs that permitted the vessel to resume its voyage.

On 26 March 2022, the Canadian Coast Guard Ship "G. PEDDLE S.C." reported that its rigid-hull inflatable boat had capsized during an exercise in the Bedford Basin off Halifax, NS. One crew member sustained minor injuries.
On 13 March 2022, the tug "COAST WOOD IX" was reported as sinking at a dock in Fraser River off Mission, BC. The vessel was retrieved and removed from the marine environment.

On 12 March 2022, the halibut fishing vessel "MUCKTOWN GIRL", with 5 people on board, reported having electrical problems 87.5 nautical miles southeast of Canso, NS. At 1608 AST the same day, while under tow by the Canadian Coast Guard Ship "JEAN GOODWILL," the towline broke free. The CCGS "JEAN GOODWILL" stood by awaiting improved weather conditions before attempting to re-establish the tow. On 13 March 2022 at 0619 ADT, the fishing vessel reported taking on water and the crew prepared to abandon ship into a life raft wearing their immersion suits. At 0803 ADT, 4 crew from the "MUCKTOWN GIRL" were rescued by the CCGS "JEAN GOODWILL". Later that day, at 1236 ADT, JRCC Halifax reported the missing crew member was recovered but did not survive.

On 23 February 2022, the fishing vessel "DUSTY JAMES", with 3 people on board, reported taking on water and being at risk of sinking in the Fraser River near Ladner, BC. The vessel was towed to a nearby marina by another fishing vessel where the crew effected repairs.

On 16 February 2022, the fishing vessel "C13146BC" known as "FORTUNE HUNTER I", with 3 people on board, reported taking on water and being at risk of sinking in Cordova Bay off Gordon Head, BC. The crew carried out repairs and the vessel was towed to Tsehum Harbour, BC by the Canadian Coast Guard Ship "CAPE CUPPER".

On 05 February 2022, the fishing vessel "TENACIOUS", with 4 people on board, reported taking on water and being at risk of sinking off Vancouver Island, BC. The crew carried out repairs and the vessel resumed its voyage to Ucluelet, BC.

On 29 December 2021, the fishing vessel "PACIFIC BANKER", with no one board, reported taking on water and being at risk of sinking while docked in Steveston Harbour in Richmond, BC. The vessel was stabilized with the assistance from the emergency response unit of the Canadian Coast Guard and repairs were carried out. Minor pollution was reported.

On 22 December 2021, the fishing vessel "ROBERT AND ARIETA", with 6 people on board, reported taking on water and being at risk of sinking 24 nautical miles SE of Shelburne, NS. The crew carried out repairs and the vessel resumed its voyage to Shelburne, NS.

On 19 December 2021, the fishing vessel "NATALIE JOY", with 2 people on board, reported taking on water and being at risk of sinking in Shelburne Harbour, NS. On 29 September 2019 at approximately 0630 MDT, the 9.1 m aluminum-fishing vessel Jamie Michelle Lynne (C18787AB) with 4 people on board departed Hay River, NT. The vessel was bound for Sulphur Point, approximately 28 mile east from Hay River. The intent of the fishing trip was to harvest the fish and remove their gill-nets from the area.  On 30 September at approximately 0900, the Jamie Michelle Lynne was reported missing on Great Slave Lake, NT. At 1225, SAR operations began. Resources deployed included TC 951 pollution surveillance aircraft, Rescue 804 twin otter aircraft and CCG 775. At 2013, the search was suspended for the day.On 01 October at 08:01, JRCC Trenton advised the search and rescue efforts for overdue vessel resumed. CGE 777 and Guardian worked in tandem, Canadian Forces Rescue 805 commenced a shore search from Lonely Bay and CASARA aircraft searched the north shore search.  TC 951 Pollution Aircraft crew was on rest and did not participate. At 1139, the capsized vessel was located near Windy Bay with approximately 1 m of the bow protruding out of the water. A search of the debris field did not locate any of the people on board. An underwater video camera was used to identify the vessel and search for bodies but the camera could not reach the cabin of the vessel.On 02 October, the weather was not conducive to an underwater camera survey of the vessel cabin. CCG and DFO vessels continued the search for the people on board. During the adverse weather conditions the vessel completely sank in approximately 40 m of water.On 03 October, the RCMP surveyed the vessel’s cabin with the underwater camera and did not locate any bodies. The 4 fish harvesters are still missing and presumed drowned.

On 03 October 2018, the fishing vessel "FORTRESS ISLE II", with 5 people on board, had water in the lazarette from an unidentified source. The water was transferred to the hold and then discharged overboard. The Canadian Coast Guard ship "W. JACKMAN" was tasked to assist.

On 15 September 2018, the fishing vessel "DADDY'S DREAM", with 2 people on board, had a damaged water intake valve and began taking on water, 7 nautical miles WNW of Old Perlican, NL.  A nearby fishing vessel "TRINITY VENTURE" towed the vessel to Old Perlican.

On 03 October 2018, an aquaculture vessel, "C11582BC", while moored and with no one on board, took on water and was at risk of sinking near Twin Island, Cortes Bay, BC. The owner dewatered the vessel at low tide.

On 03 October 2018, an aquaculture vessel, "C11582BC", while moored and with no one on board, took on water and was at risk of sinking near Twin Island, Cortes Bay, BC. The owner dewatered the vessel at low tide.

On 18 September 2018, the fishing vessel "KYLA ANNE", with 3 people on board, capsized 1.3 nautical miles north of North Cape, PE. One crewmember swam ashore and called for assistance. After an intense search and rescue effort by numerous air, sea and land assets that lasted 6 days, the other 2 crewmembers' bodies were found on the shore.

On 13 August 2018, the tug "GEORGE H LEDCOR", while towing the loaded gravel barge "EVCO 55", girded and capsized in the Fraser River, BC. On 25 July 2018, the survey vessel "C27030QC" also known as USHIK reported taking on water while approaching Sept-Iles, QC.

On 20 July 2018, the sports fishing charter vessel "BC2796102" also known as "REEL DEVIL", with 6 passengers and 1 crew onboard, took on water and capsized near Hodgson Islands, BC. The passengers and crew were rescued by another recreational craft.

On 19 July 2018, a rescue boat belonging to the passenger vessel "EXPLORER OF THE SEAS" capsized while coming alongside the passenger vessel near Ogden Point, BC. There were three people on the rescue boat. Two people were thrown overboard due to capsizing. A pilot vessel recovered the persons in water and transported them to Ogden Point, BC.
On 18 July 2018, a marine construction barge, registered as "13K81942", sank after taking on water through the hatches near Sunset Marina, Howe Sound, BC. The barge was refloated using air bags.

On 15 June 2018, the unlicensed 6.1 m aluminum fishing/harvesting vessel "C22761BC," known as “NUCHAHT,” with 5 people on board, took on water, capsized, and sank in Duffin Passage, near Tofino, BC. Two people on board who were not part of the crew managed to swim to shore. The Canadian Coast Guard (CCG) Search and Rescue conducted a search for the 3 crew, but they are still missing and presumed drowned.On 14 June 2018, at approximately 2230, the crew suspended halibut fishing operations and returned to Tofino. The crew socialized at a local establishment until 0100 on 15 June. The 3 crew and 2 other people left the establishment and returned to the vessel where they socialized until 0230 and then departed the dock. At some point during a large course alteration, the vessel capsized. Everyone on board ended up in the water.At 0306, the Joint Rescue Coordination Centre (JRCC) in Victoria received a report of persons in the water calling for help. No other distress call was received. JRCC tasked the CCG fast rescue craft Tofino 1. By 0422, the 2 people who were not crew had been located. The search for the 3 crew members continued until 2111, when the search was reduced and the case was turned over to the RCMP. The sea and weather conditions were not likely a factor and the cause of the vessel capsizing could not be determined.

On 12 July 2018, the small open boat "CLOUD NINE SALMON LODGE BOAT", with 3 people on board, was reported capsized. Two persons were recovered safe and sound from the water. The third person is missing and presumed drowned.

On 06 July 2018, the fishing vessel "MISS LORNA LEE", with 5 people on board, reported that there was water ingress in the lazarette. The vessel's pumps were working and the water ingress was under control. The Canadian Coast Guard vessel "SIR WILFRED GRENFELL" was tasked to assist and subsequently reported that the "MISS LORNA LEE" had returned to LaScie, NL.

On 29 June 2018, the fishing vessel "SARATOGA", with 5 people on board, reported that it was taking on water. The vessel's crew was keeping up with the water ingress. The Canadian Coast Guard vessel "CAPE LIGHT" transferred pumps to the "SARATOGA". The fishing vessel's crew pumped out the remaining water and proceeded to Clark's Harbour, NS.

On 26 June 2018, the fishing vessel "AVALON PRIDE", with 5 people on board, reported it had a broken rudder and was taking on water. All 5 crew members were taken on board the Canadian Coast Guard vessel "CYGNUS" and brought to Fermeuse, NL. The abandoned vessel subsequently sank. No pollution was reported.

On 16 June 2018, the charter sports fishing vessel "C13516BC", with 5 people on board, reported rapidly taking on water off shore from Tofino, BC. The vessel's pumps were unable to keep up with the water ingress. Two Canadian Coast Guard vessels escorted the vessel to Tofino, BC, where the passengers disembarked and the vessel was removed from the water.
On 31 May 2018, the fishing vessel "BAIT'EM & CRATE'EM", with 4 people on board, reported taking on water. There were no injuries or pollution reported.

On 21 May 2018, the fishing vessel "ANDRE F", with 3 people on board, reported taking on water off Huckleberry Island, NB. The vessel intentionally grounded to avoid sinking. The Canadian Coast Guard deployed a search and rescue team to the scene and provided pumps to assist the disabled vessel. The "ANDRE F" eventually refloated and was escorted to Neguac, NB by the Canadian Coast Guard vessel "CAP BRETON".

On 19 May 2018, the fishing vessel "CAN'T COMPLAIN", with 3 people on board, reported taking on water 4 nautical miles SW of Clark's Harbour, NS. The Canadian Coast Guard cutter "CAPE LIGHT" dropped off search and rescue pumps and the vessel returned to port under its own power.

On 11 May 2018, the fishing vessel "CARSON REESE", with 3 people on board, reported taking on water .5 nautical miles from Neguac, NB. The crew effected temporary repairs and the vessel returned to port unassisted.

On 13 April 2018, the fishing vessel "MAKO SHARK", with 3 people on board, reported taking on water around the rudder stock while beset in ice 1/4 nautical mile east of Bridgeport, NL. The Canadian Coast Guard ship "TERRY FOX" freed them from the ice and the vessel returned to port.

On 10 April 2018, the fishing vessel "ANYWEATHER", reported taking on water. The vessel transited to the wharf in Sandy Point, NS. The Canadian Coast Guard ship "CAPE ROGER" deployed their fast rescue craft with a pump to assist with dewatering. There were no injuries or pollution reported.

On 12 May 2018, the fishing vessel "OCEAN STAR II", with 3 people on board, was reported as capsized 1.57 nautical miles NE of Black Point, NS and 0.05 nautical miles from the nearest shoreline. One of the crew members was able to swim to shore and the other 2 were found non-responsive at the shoreline. Several fishing vessels arrived to assist but were unable to land on the shoreline. One vessel called 911 to request assistance. The survivor walked to a nearby house to get help. A third fishing vessel intentionally grounded to get a crew member ashore to provide assistance to the 2 non-responsive crew members.

On 03 May 2018, the fishing vessel "DIVERCITY", with 3 people on board, reported taking on water due to a holed hull while in the Estevan Sound, BC. The vessel was towed to Port Edward by an assisting vessel.

On 07 May 2018, the fishing vessel "C16769BC", known as "DEVIL FISH", with no one on board, was reported as sinking while being towed by the fishing vessel "MAJESTIC WARRIOR" to Cape Calvert in Queen Charlotte Sound, BC. The towed vessel "DEVIL FISH" was being used as a storage vessel for traps by the fishing vessel "MAJESTIC WARRIOR".

On 08 May 2018, the fishing vessel "TRINA MARGARET", with 4 people on board, was reported as capsized 2.0 nautical miles north off Point Escuminac, NB. Three of the people on board entered the water and held on to the overturned vessel until they were recovered by another fishing vessel. The remaining person was able to walk on the vessel's hull as it capsized and was recovered from the bottom of the overturned vessel without entering the water. All 4 people on board were taken to the wharf at Point Escuminac, NB, and transported to hospital where they were assessed for hypothermia and released. No other injuries or pollution were reported.

On 05 May 2018, the "UNNAMED 19 FOOT FISHING VESSEL", with 2 people on board, was found capsized 0.04 nautical miles NE of Beach Cove Point, Port Medway, NS. A search of the area was launched. The deckhand was found non-responsive on the shoreline approximately 0.08 nautical miles east of the overturned vessel. The deckhand was transported to hospital by ambulance and later pronounced dead. The master's body was recovered with some fishing gear near the overturned vessel later the same day. The overturned vessel was towed to the public wharf and removed from the water.

On 19 April 2018, the barge "S.N. 4" was reported sunk while tied to the dock in Snug Basin, near Port Alberni, BC. No pollution reported.

On 07 March 2017, the fishing vessel "NAFCO", with 3 people on board, reported taking on water in the Strait of Georgia, BC. The pumps in the engine room kept up with the ingress of water as the vessel proceeded to Steveston, BC.

On 18 January 2017, the work boat "C21361BC", with no one on board, capsized while moored in Kelsey Bay, BC. The vessel was recovered and removed from the marine environment by the owner.

Marie, ON. The crew members were immediately retrieved from the water and sustained minor injuries.There was no damage and no pollution.

On 03 December 2016, the fishing vessel "MISS LITTLE RIVER", with 5 people on board, reported taking on water 23 nautical miles WSW of Cape Forchu, NS. There were no injuries or pollution reported.

On 01 December 2016, the fishing vessel "TIDE "N" KNOTS", with 5 people on board, reported taking on water 17 nautical miles west of Chebogue Point, NS. The vessel subsequently received a pump from a search and rescue aircraft and was escorted to port by the Canadian Coast Guard cutter "GELIGET".

On 27 November 2016, the tug "PEACE BOOMER 4", while being towed to a work site by the tug "JENNELL II",  took on water and sank in Howe Sound, BC. The tug "PEACE BOOMER 4" did not have any fuel on board and there was no pollution.

On 07 November 2016, the research vessel "ARCTIC PROWLER", while berthed at the Saint Lunaire, NL community wharf and with no one on board, started taking on water. The local fire department stopped the leak and dewatered the vessel. There was minimal damage, no injuries or pollution reported.

There were minor injuries and some damage reported but no pollution.

On 21 October 2016, the fishing vessel "LATITUDE ADJUSTMENT", with 5 people on board, was reported as taking on water and sinking. On 11 October 2016, the fishing vessel "NO EXCUSES", with 5 people on board, reported taking on water and having broken its wheelhouse windows 22 nautical miles south of Sable Island, NS. On 14 October 2016, the workboat "C20927BC" was reported as sunk while tied to a barge at a fish farm in Clayoquot Sound, BC. No injuries or pollution reported.

On 06 September 2016, the small 22 foot fishing vessel "POP'S PRIDE", with 4 people on board, was reported overdue after it did not return to St. John's, NL from the fishing grounds off Cape Spear, NL. Several vessels participated in a search where 2 people were recovered deceased. The submerged vessel was recovered the following day. Two people were not recovered and are presumed drowned.

On 05 September 2016, the fishing vessel "BIG BUDDY", with 4 people on board, was reported taking on water and in danger of sinking. The intake of water was controlled by the crew. No injury or pollution was reported.

On 14 May 2016, the fishing vessel "FIONA B", with 3 people on board, reported taking on water 2.7 nautical miles NE of Cape Gabarus, NS. On 12 May 2016, the fishing vessel "MA BELLE II" reported taking on water 25 nautical miles east of Miscou Island, NB. The vessel was subsequently escorted to port by the Canadian Coast Guard cutter "CAP BRETON".

No injuries or pollution reported.

On 26 August 2016, the fishing vessel "TYLER", was reported to be taking on water about 70 nautical miles WSW of Yarmouth, NS. The crew controlled the intake of water on board. No injury or pollution was reported.

On 09 August 2016, the fishing vessel "ROBIN", with 5 people on board, reported taking on water 5.8 nautical miles north of Shemogue Head, NB. The vessel was subsequently de-watered and towed to port by the Canadian Coast Guard cutter "CAP NORD".

On 01 August 2016, the fishing vessel "LITTLE JACK", with 5 people on board, reported taking on water and in danger of sinking. The crew stopped the leak and the vessel proceeded to Fortune, NL. No injury or pollution was reported.

On 26 August 2016, the fishing vessel "NANCY LYNN", with no one on board, was reported as taking on water while secured at a dock in Bella Bella, BC. The Bella Bella lifeboat's crew stabilized the vessel and another fishing vessel towed the vessel "NANCY LYNN" to Shearwater, BC for repair. Minor pollution reported.

On 24 August 2016, the fishing vessel "LE PIRATE DES MERS ", with 4 people on board, reported taking on water 7.7 nautical miles east of Miscou Island, NB. The vessel was later assisted and towed to Miscou Island, NB.

On 25 July 2016, the passenger/cargo vessel "C12183BC", known as "SKYDIVER", sank after taking on water in Georgia Strait, BC. The crew abandoned the vessel and were rescued by a vessel of opportunity. Deck cargo of PVC pipes and 100 litres of fuel oil were released into the sea. There were no injuries reported.

On 24 June 2016, the fishing vessel "TWIN STARRS II", with 1 person on board, began taking on water into the lazarette space near Ucluelet, BC. The vessel proceeded to Ucluelet, BC and the crew pumped the water out using additional pumps.

On 16 June 2016, the fishing vessel "C19496NB", with 3 people on board, took water over the stern and capsized while hauling a lobster trap snarled with other lobster gear about .5 nautical miles west of Miller Brook Wharf, NB. The fishing vessel "MARIE ELISER 1" rescued a deckhand and later recovered the other two crew members. The rescue vessel returned the vessel's crew to Miller Brook Wharf, NB where the only survivor was transported to the hospital. There were 2 fatalities.

On 11 April 2016, the fishing vessel "JASON & CHRISTY", with 3 people on board, was reported taking on water 8 nautical miles SW of Clark's Harbour, NS. The vessel was subsequently escorted to port by the Canadian Coast Guard cutter "CLARK'S HARBOUR".

On 01 April 2016, the tug "OCEAN UANNAQ" capsized while attempting to move a barge with 2 other tugs to L’Île-des-Sœurs, QC during construction of the new Champlain bridge on the St. Lawrence River off Montréal, QC. On 22 March 2016, the fishing vessel "KOKANEE" reported taking on water and at risk of sinking while moored at Port Hardy, BC. The vessel was de-watered with portable pumps and will be hauled out of the water. Minor pollution was reported.

On 19 September 2004, the small fishing vessel Ryan's Commander departed Bay de Verde, Newfoundland and Labrador, for a trip to its home port of St. Brendan's (Cottel Island), Newfoundland and Labrador. The trip was uneventful as the vessel proceeded on a northerly course with the wind and seas on the starboard bow. At approximately 1800 Newfoundland daylight time, the vessel was about seven nautical miles east-southeast of Cape Bonavista, Newfoundland and Labrador, and the course was altered toward the northwest. During the next 30 minutes, with the vessel running beam to gale-force winds and sea, it experienced three heavy rolls to port. It recovered from the first two; however, the third roll left the vessel on its beam-ends. A distress message was transmitted and the crew of six abandoned ship into an inflatable liferaft. One crew member was subsequently rescued from the liferaft by a search and rescue helicopter. The remaining five crew members were thrown from the liferaft into the water as it came ashore. Three survived; two did not

On 19 June 2004, a public activity day featuring a rafting excursion was organized on the Magog River in Sherbrooke, Quebec. The first raft left with nine passengers and a guide aboard. Less than one minute after departing, the raft struck a rock and capsized, sending all occupants into the water.The guide and two passengers quickly climbed onto the overturned raft, which continued its descent. Two other passengers were able to cling to rocks, and a fifth passenger was recovered upstream from the last ledge. Carried by the current, three other passengers descended the river and reached the raft that, following its descent, was purposely run aground on the bank downstream from the rapids.A ninth passenger remained stuck and submerged under a rock 5 m downstream from the point of capsizing. He was found some 1 hour and 30 minutes later and pronounced dead at the hospital.

On the evening of 16 June 2004, the Persistence I sailed from Baie-du-Renard, Quebec, on Anticosti Island, Quebec, on a course to Natashquan, Quebec. En route, the seawater circulation system for the live-well tanks was started to preserve the catch. After a few hours under way, the operator noticed that the fishing vessel was not handling as usual. Upon conducting an inspection, he discovered that the after part of the vessel had settled lower in the water and that water had flooded into the aft compartments. The operator broadcast an urgency communication prefixed PAN PAN.The Marine Communications and Traffic Services at Rivière-au-Renard, Quebec, received the message and transmitted a Mayday Relay. A search and rescue operation was launched that included a Canadian Coast Guard ship (CCGS), and a Canadian Forces aircraft and helicopter. The CCGS Cap de Rabast and the Violaine.C.I located the Persistence I and escorted it to Natashquan. Although the afterdeck was gradually sinking below the surface, the operator managed to reach port at Natashquan and to beach the vessel near the wharf at 0525 eastern daylight time on June 17.

On 27 September 2003, during a voyage from Bas Caraquet, New Brunswick, to Makkovik, Labrador, the fishing vessel Evan Richard, with three persons on board, dropped anchor a few hundred metres off the coast of Anticosti Island, Quebec. On 29 September, the crew was awakened by strong winds from the south-southeast. The weather was deteriorating rapidly with the approach of the tropical storm Juan.During a manoeuvre to leave the anchorage, the boat started to ship water. A short time later, the after deck was flooded and a Mayday was broadcast as the Evan Richard quickly settled. The occupants sought refuge on top of the wheelhouse which was the only part of the vessel still above water. While attempting to swim to the inflatable boat that the Evan Richard was towing as a lifeboat, the master fell in the water and drifted towards the island.The Evan Richard was driven onto the beach of Anticosti Island about 3 nautical miles from the position where the Mayday was broadcast. The master was picked up on the shore by a Search and Rescue helicopter, but the other two persons are still missing.

On the morning of 1 March 1999, the herring seiner Westisle was experiencing rough seas off the west coast of Vancouver Island. Seawater shipped on deck, down flooded past an improperly secured aluminum fish-loading deck scuttle cover leading to the forward starboard cargo tank, causing a starboard list. Down flooding into the compartment increased when the cover became dislodged. When the unsecured deck cargo shifted suddenly to starboard, the vessel was reportedly heeled to an angle of about 70º. By ballasting and moving weights, the crew was able to return the vessel to a near upright position. Damage to the vessel was limited to seawater contamination of the main engine fuel injectors and fuel system. No injuries or pollution resulted from this occurrence.

On 27 November 1998, while crossing between Les Escoumins and Rimouski, Quebec, in foul weather, the master of the scallop dragger "BRIER MIST" informed the Marine Communications and Traffic Services that he thought the hold and afterpeak were taking on water and that the pumps were not able to cope with it. At about 1500, the vessel foundered some 10 nautical miles off Rimouski. Despite the search and rescue operations, no trace of the wreck or of three of the five crew members was found. The two recovered victims had drowned. Section 3 of this report contains the Board's findings as to causes and contributing factors and other findings. In Section 4, the Board has identified safety deficiencies related to the inspection of hatch covers on small fishing vessels, the absence of automatic release mechanisms on liferafts and the absence of emergency position indicating radio beacons. The Board has issued four safety recommendations to address these safety deficiencies. The Board is concerned by the lack of safety action taken following recommendations previously issued by the Board on water level detectors, protection from hypothermia and drowning, and marine emergency duties training for fishermen, and recommendations on the same issues by the Chief Coroner as a result of this accident. Section 4 also lists the relevant safety action taken by Transport Canada, the Quebec Chief Coroner's Office and the TSB.

Before the vessel recovered, another steep wave struck the "TWIN J." and caused it to capsize to starboard. The crew was thrown into the water but soon boarded a self-inflated liferaft. Some 6 hours later the raft was located by a United States Coast Guard rescue plane. The survivors were rescued by a United States fishing vessel approximately 12 hours after the capsizing. No injuries or pollution were reported as a result of the accident. .

The vessel, with three passengers and an operator on board, departed Tofino, British Columbia, on a three-hour trip to watch marine life. All wore "coverall PFD (personal flotation device) suits"; while the passengers' suits were properly worn, the operator's suit was partially zipped. After watching whales, the operator decided to show the passengers marine life in the vicinity of Plover Reefs. While in that area, the boat was swamped and broached by a large swell, which threw all the occupants into the turbulent water. The rapidity of the occurrence precluded transmission of a Mayday message. When the boat did not arrive at its destination, the owner initiated Search and Rescue action. Two passengers were rescued after about two hours. The operator and one passenger lost their lives. The Board determined that the "OCEAN THUNDER" was swamped and rolled suddenly to a large angle, throwing all occupants into the cold water. A factor contributing to the occurrence was that the operator did not fully appreciate the conditions the boat would meet at the time of the accident in the turbulent waters in the vicinity of reefs. Contributing to the loss of lives were: anxiety associated with sudden immersion in cold water, the lack of effective communication equipment, and the absence of emergency (medium range) communication equipment, which resulted in a delay in initiating a Search and Rescue response.

In the early hours of 02 December 1997, while bringing on board the final haul of a herring trawling voyage, the small fishing vessel "PACIFIC CHARMER" slowly heeled to starboard before downflooding and sinking in about 55 metres of water in Pylades Channel, B.C. The sea and weather conditions at the time were calm. Two of the vessel's crew and a Department of Fisheries and Oceans observer were rescued. The remaining two crew members succumbed to hypothermia and drowning.The vessel initially heeled to starboard because her intact transverse stability had been reduced by the cumulative detrimental effects of the weight of additional and spare fishing gear; asymmetric loading; free surface effects of liquids in partially filled tanks and fish holds; and fish waste water retained on deck. The dynamic effects of the weight of the trawl net cod-end being briefly suspended from a winch located above the wheel-house caused a sudden rise in the vessel's virtual centre of gravity. In conjunction with the initial small heel to starboard, the dynamic effects were such that the vessel heeled further to starboard and remained briefly at an angle of about 40 degrees. Seawater shipped at this time downflooded through open weathertight doorways until all reserve buoyancy was lost and the "PACIFIC CHARMER" sank.

In order to relieve the pilot who had been on duty from Les Escoumins, Quebec, aboard the "NAVIOS MINERVA", the pilot boat "NAVIMAR V" came alongside the bulk carrier while passing the pilot station at Québec, Quebec, shortly before 0100. Two pilots from the Québec / Trois-Rivières sector climbed onto the accommodation ladder, but before they could reach the vessel's deck, the pilot boat plunged into the sea and resurfaced upside down. The master of the pilot boat was trapped in a compartment and the deckhand was thrown overboard. The Canadian Coast Guard Ship "STERNE", which was dispatched to the scene, recovered the deck-hand, who had climbed onto the overturned hull, and the master, who had swum to the surface. The "STERNE" took the survivors to the Canadian Coast Guard base, where an ambulance was waiting to take them to hospital. Both crew members were suffering from hypothermia and nervous shock, but they were released from hospital a few hours later. The "NAVIMAR V" drifted in the St. Lawrence River before sinking off the mouth of the Saint-Charles River, in about 30 metres of water. The pollution caused by the pilot boat was deemed minor. The Board determined that the pilot boat "NAVIMAR V" overturned because when she came alongside the "NAVIOS MINERVA", she overtook a wave generated by the ship, pitched onto the wave crest then surged down into the trough of the next wave before plunging into the sea. The submerged bow slowed down the pilot boat but, due to her momentum, she continued to pitch until the vessel turned over. The decision to use the accommodation ladder instead of the vessel's pilot ladder contributed to the sequence of events.

On 22 January 1997 the fishing vessel "SCOTIA GOLD" departed Digby, Nova Scotia, for Deer Island, New Brunswick. While crossing the Bay of Fundy in rough weather, the vessel began to take on water which both the vessel's main bilge pump, and the portable de-watering pump carried on board, failed to pump out. A Canadian Coast Guard Cutter, the "CUMELLA", and a Coast Guard helicopter were dispatched to the scene. The helicopter supplied a portable de-watering pump made by the same manufacturer as the vessel's portable pump; it also failed. The "CUMELLA" escorted the "SCOTIA GOLD" to Dipper Harbour, New Brunswick, where the situation was stabilized and the flood water pumped out. The Board determined that the "SCOTIA GOLD" took on water through poorly secured deck hatches. Displaced cover plates in the fish hold permitted ice slurry to enter the shaft tunnel/drain well, block the suction line to the main bilge pump and render the pump ineffective. As a result of previously undetected corrosion or damage, the portable de-watering pumps failed to operate. The portable pumps were not designed for the type of marine operation in which they were employed.

On 02 August 1996, the tug "WELDWOOD 19" was pushing a flat-topped barge with two tandem-axle dump trucks on deck. The tugmaster noticed that the barge's draught had increased and that the barge was developing a starboard list. He repositioned the trucks on the deck to counter the list and decided to turn the barge to starboard toward the shore. While making this turn, the barge developed a steadily increasing port list before striking an underwater rock and coming to a stop. The port list increased to the point where the trucks and their cargo of asphalt slid over the port side as the barge sank in about five metres of water. The tugmaster sustained a minor injury, and the asphalt caused some pollution.

On 20 June 1996, a group consisting of six inexperienced kayakers in five kayaks and one guide in a sixth kayak set out from the wharf of the Bic marina bound for the beach of Anse aux Bouleaux at the western end of Bic Harbour. The distance to be travelled was approximately 1.5 miles. While the group was en route to its destination, a north-easterly wind came up and capsized all the kayaks except the guide's. The guide managed to reach land to telephone for help, bringing one of the kayakers along with him. Meanwhile, the other kayakers managed to reach the shore on their own before help could arrive. No one was seriously injured as a result of this occurrence.

While under way from Sooke, B.C., to Bamfield, B.C., in rough weather, on 10 December 1995, the fishing vessel "DALEWOOD PROVIDER" took on water, and at about 0930, capsized. All three crew members donned survival suits, abandoned the vessel and boarded a self-inflated raft. The overturned vessel and the raft drifted apart. The raft was then swamped and overturned by a high wave, throwing all occupants in the water. Only one of them reached shore safely, while the other two drowned. Their bodies were recovered some time later. The wreck of the overturned vessel was found the next day, stranded and wedged between large rocks.

As they entered the main part of the lake, one of the small craft was swamped by high waves and subsequently capsized. A second craft swamped and capsized after it had rescued the persons from the first capsizing. The third craft made it to shore after also being swamped. Of the 12 persons aboard the three craft, 4 survived, 3 lost their lives and their bodies were recovered, and 5 were not located after extensive searches from the air, on shore and under water.

The "CHARLOTTE EXPLORER 4" (CE4) and its two occupants were declared overdue when the small boat did not return to the mother ship "CHARLOTTE EXPLORER" on the evening of 12 September 1995. A search initiated by the crew of the mother ship using other small craft continued throughout the night. At dawn, more boats and a helicopter joined the search. The "CE4" was found upside down on a beach on the north-west corner of Hippa Island. Soon afterward, the crew of the helicopter sighted the bodies of the small boat's two occupants in a kelp bed just off the coast. The Board determined that the chartered "CE4", while fishing alone with the outboard motor most likely stopped, capsized after drifting into an area of kelp and rocks where a combination of tide and sea swell was locally creating large waves of up to, or larger than, seven metres with breaking crests. The charter company's procedures with regard to fishing alone, maintaining regular radio contact and patrols to ensure the safety of its guests were not enforced. There was delay in determining that the small boat was overdue and in starting a search. As there was no witness, the exact location, time and cause of the capsizing could not be determined.

On the morning of 29 August 1995, in calm and clear weather conditions in Johnstone Straits, the fishing vessel "INSKIP" suddenly capsized at about 0835(1) when a catch of salmon being lifted over the stern slid to port. Downflooding of the fish holds caused the wooden seiner to sink quickly as she was already fully laden with fish caught earlier. The crew and the skipper's family who lived on the "INSKIP" boarded the skiff being towed alongside and were rescued by another fishing vessel in the vicinity. Minor injuries were sustained by one crew member who was pinned to the bulwark when the fish catch slid over to port.

On the evening of 23 August 1995, the twin-hulled "SHOWBOAT" departed the eastern end of Ontario Place with 39 persons aboard, 6 of whom were crew members. About 10 minutes later, both engines failed and the vessel started to list to starboard. While moving ahead at a slow speed, the "SHOWBOAT" struck a sea wall causing many of those on board to lose their footing. The vessel heeled to starboard, the starboard main deck edge became submerged, and all on board fell into the water. The vessel downflooded, sank and settled upright on the bottom in 1.8 metres of water. All on board were rescued and assisted to shore by the crew, the public and Ontario Place personnel. The Board determined that the uninspected "SHOWBOAT" was heavily laden, downflooding and slowly sinking before it struck the sea wall. There was no life-saving equipment on the vessel, but all on board were rescued promptly because the vessel sank close to shore in relatively shallow water. Contributing to the accident was the absence of clearly defined responsibility for the management of safety and for maintenance, the lack of guidance to the operators regarding the weight the vessel could carry safely, and the modification to the vessel's transom through which water downflooded.

On 06 August 1995, the self-dumping log barge "SEA-LINK RIGGER" capsized during the unloading operation. When the load of logs would not dump, preparations were begun to bring the barge back to the upright and unload by crane. The load then started to dump, but the barge was not ejected from under the load and was rolled over onto its beam ends and capsized. Two crew members from the towing tug were on board the barge; the deck-hand was rescued from the water, but the mate had to escape from a pump-room of the overturned barge. The barge was declared a total loss after it sank in deep water during subsequent salvage attempts. The Board determined that the "SEA-LINK RIGGER" capsized when, in a ballasted condition, it did not separate from a slow-dumping load of high-specific-gravity logs and the dynamics of the dumping operation rolled the barge past its beam ends. During the capsizing, a crew member from the tug "ARCTIC HOOPER" became trapped in a pump-room of the overturned barge because personnel were required to proceed below decks to control ballasting operations

The United States fishing vessel "COURAGEOUS", which was proceeding from Gig Harbour, Washington, to Ketchikan, Alaska, at the start of the fishing season, capsized in the early hours of 20 June 1995 while transiting Johnstone Strait. The vessel is believed to have been caught in a tide rip off Edith Point. As the capsizing was sudden and unexpected, only a partial distress message could be broadcast. One of the six crew members, who was sleeping in a bunk within the forecastle, was trapped in the capsized hull and lost his life. The vessel was salvaged and taken to Campbell River, B.C. It was docked and readied for towing to the United States, where it was subsequently taken.

On 01 May 1995, the service vessel "VÉZINA NO. 1" was participating in the towing of the "CAVALIER MAXIM" and was assisting the "SERVICE BOAT II". The crew of the "VÉZINA NO. 1", which was on the port quarter of the "CAVALIER MAXIM", hooked the eye of the tow-line over the single towing bitt in the middle of the afterdeck. During the inbound towage toward Louise Basin, the operator of the "VÉZINA NO. 1" tried to turn his boat 180 degrees to port as he intended to let his vessel be drawn backward. When the "VÉZINA NO. 1" executed this manoeuvre, she became girded on her starboard side and was unable to return to the upright. As a result of this and of the momentum of the tow, the "VÉZINA NO. 1" downflooded and capsized. The operator was unable to exit the wheel-house and he lost his life. The Board determined that the capsizing of the "VÉZINA NO. 1" was initially the result of the manner in which the manoeuvre was attempted. In addition, the tow-line used for the towing operation was too short and the angle between the two attachment points was clearly too steep. Since the eye of the tow-line had been hooked over the towing bitt of the "VÉZINA NO. 1", the crew members were unable to keep control of the tow-line at all times, and they were unable to release it in case of emergency.

The Hili-Kum departed from an anchorage off Moresby Island, B.C., with a cargo of red urchins for discharge at Port Edward, B.C. En route, the weather deteriorated. On 10 April 1995, in following gale- to storm-force winds and rough seas, the vessel shipped large volumes of water on the afterdeck, settled by the stern, and sank stern first. The three crew members donned immersion suits, abandoned the vessel, and boarded a liferaft. Two of the three immersion suits were defective, and the liferaft capsized several times. Two of the crew succumbed to hypothermia and drowned; the survivor was rescued some five and a half hours later.The Board determined that the Hili-Kum proceeded to sea despite a storm warning broadcast, and was being operated in following high winds and rough seas with the fish hold hatch cover not battened down. The cumulative effect of large volumes of seawater shipped on the afterdeck, the vessel's low freeboard aft, and the flooding/downflooding of the below-deck spaces aft caused the vessel to settle by the stern, lose reserve buoyancy, and sink stern first. The hypothermia and subsequent drowning of two of the crew is attributable to the poor state of repair of their immersion suits and to their exposure to the harsh weather conditions when the liferaft capsized.

In the early morning hours of 11 February 1995, the "PACIFIC BANDIT", laden with about 23,000 kg of fish, was off the west coast of Vancouver Island, British Columbia, not engaged in fishing operations. The wind and sea conditions were such that the vessel was shipping and retaining seas on the main deck. The vessel listed to starboard, downflooded, capsized, and eventually sank. Two crew members were swept overboard; the other two abandoned the vessel and managed to board the liferaft. Three of the crew members were later rescued and one person, who was in the water without a lifejacket or an immersion suit, succumbed to hypothermia and drowned.The Board determined that, while operating in moderate sea conditions, the "PACIFIC BANDIT" capsized when positive transverse stability was lost due to the cumulative effect of the shipped seas retained on deck, the stowage of the catch, the free surface effect of liquids, and downflooding to the below-deck spaces. The open weathertight doors and the broken galley windows accelerated the downflooding, which continued until the vessel lost all reserve buoyancy and sank.

On the morning of 11 August 1994, the fishing vessel "MISS STEPHANIE II", while retrieving fish from trap nets, shipped water on her afterdeck and in the aftermost under-deck compartment. While the vessel's afterdeck was submerged, the net was let go and the vessel headed toward shore. A short time later, the "MISS STEPHANIE II" sank stern first. Two guests drowned; however, five crew members survived. The Board determined that the "MISS STEPHANIE II" was lost following an accumulation of water in the lazaret, which could not be discharged due to an inoperative bilge pump. Subsequent progressive flooding of the engine-room led to the loss of reserve buoyancy and longitudinal stability which resulted in the sudden stern-first sinking.

The "LADY DEVINE", heavily laden with prawn traps, was struck on the port quarter by a large swell and capsized. The two crew members climbed up on the hull and waited for rescue, but the vessel drifted in a westerly direction and grounded in Forward Bay, British Columbia. The two crew members suffered from hypothermia and the deck-hand later drowned. The owner/operator was stranded on West Cracroft Island, British Columbia, for two days before the "LADY DEVINE" was sighted by a passing vessel and he was rescued. The Board determined that the effective after freeboard and transverse stability of the "LADY DEVINE" were markedly reduced due to the number of prawn traps stowed on the afterdeck. The weather deteriorated later in the day and stabilizers were not deployed. The stacked prawn traps and a nylon tarpaulin presented a large surface area to the strong wind and acted like a large sail retarding the vessel's return to the upright. The vessel shipped and retained water on the weather deck, downflooded, and capsized to starboard. Seawater entered the forward under-deck compartments through the open door at the after end of the wheel-house and through the fish hold when the unsecured fish hold hinged hatch cover became displaced.

Nine sea-kayak charterers, led by two guides, were on passage to Vertical Point, Louise Island, B.C. On encountering adverse weather conditions near Heming Head, four kayaks were overwhelmed and capsized. Two members of the group were rescued immediately and two others were swept away by the waves. They were discovered in the water three hours later during a Search and Rescue mission. One was suffering from acute hypothermia. The other was later determined to have died from hypothermia and drowning. The Board determined that the inexperienced group attempted a sea journey even though they were under-trained to safely handle their craft and to cope with emergencies, and were ill-prepared for the open water conditions which could be expected from the weather forecast. The fact that group discipline was not enforced and that the Search and Rescue mission was delayed because of initial confusion in the group and radio communications difficulties contributed to the death of one member of the group.

On 05 July 1993, the 5.5-metre open fishing vessel CFV #132145 capsized when struck broadside by a wave as a lobster trap was being reset. The three occupants, who were not wearing lifejackets or personal flotation devices (PFDs), were thrown into the water. After the owner/operator had assisted his son and grandson on to the overturned boat, he lost consciousness, was washed off the boat, and disappeared. The two men stayed with the boat, which drifted to an island where they huddled in a rock crevice until rescued the next morning. The Board determined that the boat capsized when she was struck broadside by a breaking sea, the dynamic forces of which she was unable to withstand because of the unequal distribution of weight on board.

In the early morning hours of 05 July 1993, in deteriorating weather conditions, the "E.L.M." abandoned a routine fishing trip in the Minas Basin, Nova Scotia, with the intention of seeking shelter. Shipping water heavily, the "E.L.M." subsequently swamped and sank while attempting to beach in shallow water. One of the crew members became trapped in the vessel's rigging and drowned; the two remaining crew members were rescued uninjured. The Board determined that the "E.L.M." sank because structural changes carried out when the vessel was converted to stern trawling made her vulnerable to shipping seas and, in the prevailing rough weather, progressive flooding continued until all reserve buoyancy was lost.

While crossing Skidegate Narrows, British Columbia, the "CROWN FOREST 72-68" listed to starboard until the vessel capsized. The crew of two was in the wheel-house. The operator escaped from the wheel-house and climbed on the capsized hull. He was unable to find his companion after a search above and below water. The operator was rescued a short time later. The body of the missing crew member was later recovered from the wheel-house by a diver but resuscitation attempts were unsuccessful. The Board determined that the vessel capsized because of a loss of initial transverse stability due to the free-surface effect of water accumulating on deck. The water accumulation was caused primarily by the deteriorated condition of the bow ramp seal. The fact that the vessel's operators and managers were not sufficiently knowledgeable to recognize that the ineffective ramp/hull seal seriously compromised the vessel's stability, and that no action was taken on unsafe condition reports made by the vessel's operators following previous near-capsizings contributed to this accident.

On 11 May 1993, the fishing vessel "WHISKEY JACK" was engaged in seafood harvesting and anchored in the shallow waters off Fan Island, Porcher Peninsula, British Columbia. While the heavily laden "WHISKEY JACK" was in the process of weighing anchor, a succession of large waves struck on her port quarter. The vessel shipped large quantities of water causing her to rapidly settle by the stern and founder. One of the three crew members succumbed to hypothermia and drowned, and the two others were rescued suffering from hypothermia. The Board determined that the heavily laden "WHISKEY JACK" was swamped by successive large waves and foundered. Valuable time was lost because the Search and Rescue (SAR) initiative was prematurely terminated at the communication stage as a result of confusion regarding the identity of the vessel in distress. This confusion arose from the fact that two vessels had transmitted similar MAYDAY messages almost simultaneously.
